## 2 Set Up

The purpose of this section is to introduce the double null formalism adapted to the setting of straight self-similar spacetimes. We also introduce the commutation formulas and the error term notation that we use later.

### 2.1 Double Null Gauge

We introduce a double null gauge on the $(n+2)$ -dimensional manifold $\big(\mathcal{M},g\big)$ following the work of [RSR18, Section 3]. In this section we consider a general such foliation, in order to define the relevant quantities and write down the system of Einstein vacuum equations (1.10) in double null gauge. In the next section we will use the additional assumptions of self-similarity and straightness, which simplify our equations. We assume for the purpose of this section that $g$ is smooth, and we later define the notion of regular vacuum solution in Definition 2.2. Our introduction of the double null gauge will be brief, and we encourage the reader to consult [RSR18, Section 3] for complete statements and proofs.

We assume our background differentiable manifold to be $\big((-\infty,0]\times[0,\infty)\backslash\{(0,0)\}\big)\times S^{n},$ where the coordinates $(u,v)$ parameterize $(-\infty,0]\times[0,\infty)\backslash\{(0,0)\}.$ We consider the metric $g$ in double null gauge:

$$ g=-2\Omega^{2}(du\otimes dv+dv\otimes du)+\not{g}_{AB}(d\theta^{A}-b^{A}du)\otimes(d\theta^{B}-b^{B}du), $$

where $\{\theta^{A}\}$ represent local coordinates on $S^{n}.$ We denote $S_{u,v}=\{u\}\times\{v\}\times S^{n}.$ We define the normalized frame:

$$ e_{3}=\Omega^{-1}(\partial_{u}+b^{A}\partial_{A}),\ e_{4}=\Omega^{-1}\partial_{v},\ g(e_{3},e_{4})=-2. $$

We denote by $D$ the Levi-Civita connection of $\big(\mathcal{M},g\big)$ . Following [RSR18, Section 3] and the references therein, we introduce the notion of horizontal tensors on $S_{u,v}$ , with entries in the tangent space of $S_{u,v}$ , and we denote by $\nabla_{A},\ \nabla_{3},\ \nabla_{4}$ the projections of $D_{A},\ D_{3},\ D_{4}$ to the tangent space of $S_{u,v}$ , for any vector $e_{A}$ tangent to $S_{u,v}$ .

We define the Ricci coefficients denoted schematically by $\psi\in\{\chi,\underline{\chi},\eta,\underline{\eta},\omega,\underline{\omega},\zeta\}$ as:

$$ \displaystyle\chi_{AB}=g(D_{A}e_{4},e_{B}),\ \underline{\chi}_{AB}=g(D_{A}e_{3},e_{B}),\ \eta_{A}=-\frac{1}{2}g(D_{3}e_{A},e_{4}),\ \underline{\eta}_{A}=-\frac{1}{2}g(D_{4}e_{A},e_{3}) \displaystyle\omega=-\frac{1}{4}g(D_{4}e_{3},e_{4}),\ \underline{\omega}=-\frac{1}{4}g(D_{3}e_{4},e_{3}),\ \zeta_{A}=\frac{1}{2}g(D_{A}e_{4},e_{3}). $$

We decompose $\chi$ and $\underline{\chi}$ as:

$$ \chi_{AB}=\hat{\chi}_{AB}+\frac{1}{n}\text{tr}\chi\not{g}_{AB},\ \underline{\chi}_{AB}=\underline{\hat{\chi}}_{AB}+\frac{1}{n}\text{tr}\underline{\chi}\not{g}_{AB}. $$

As proved in [RSR18, Section 3], we have the Ricci formulas:

$$ \displaystyle D_{4}e_{4}=-2\omega e_{4},\ D_{4}e_{3}=2\omega e_{3}+2\underline{\eta}^{A}e_{A},\ D_{4}e_{A}=\underline{\eta}_{A}e_{4}+\nabla_{4}e_{A} \displaystyle D_{3}e_{3}=-2\underline{\omega}e_{3},\ D_{3}e_{4}=2\underline{\omega}e_{4}+2\eta^{A}e_{A},\ D_{3}e_{A}=\eta_{A}e_{3}+\nabla_{3}e_{A} \displaystyle D_{A}e_{4}=-\zeta_{A}e_{4}+\chi_{A}^{B}e_{B},\ D_{A}e_{3}=\zeta_{A}e_{3}+\underline{\chi}_{A}^{B}e_{B},\ D_{A}e_{B}=\frac{1}{2}\underline{\chi}e_{4}+\frac{1}{2}\chi e_{3}+\nabla_{A}e_{B}. $$

We also have the metric equations:

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{4}\not{g}_{AB}=2\chi_{AB},\ \mathcal{L}_{3}\not{g}_{AB}=2\underline{\chi}_{AB},\ \omega=-\frac{1}{2}\nabla_{4}\log\Omega,\ \underline{\omega}=-\frac{1}{2}\nabla_{3}\log\Omega \displaystyle\zeta_{A}=-\frac{1}{4}\Omega^{-1}\not{g}_{AB}e_{4}(b^{B}),\ \eta_{A}=\zeta_{A}+\nabla_{A}\log\Omega,\ \underline{\eta}_{A}=-\zeta_{A}+\nabla_{A}\log\Omega. $$

We define the curvature components denoted schematically by $\Psi\in\{\alpha,\underline{\alpha},\beta,\underline{\beta},\nu,\underline{\nu},\sigma,\rho,\tau\}:$

$$ \displaystyle\alpha_{AB}=R_{A4B4},\ \underline{\alpha}_{AB}=R_{A3B3},\ \beta_{A}=\frac{1}{2}R_{A434},\ \underline{\beta}_{A}=\frac{1}{2}R_{A334},\ \nu_{ABC}=R_{ABC4},\ \underline{\nu}_{ABC}=R_{ABC3} \displaystyle\sigma_{AB}=\frac{1}{2}R_{3A4B}-\frac{1}{2}R_{3B4A},\ \tau_{AB}=\frac{1}{2}R_{3A4B}+\frac{1}{2}R_{3B4A},\ \rho=\frac{1}{4}R_{4343} $$

As proved in [RSR18, Section 3], we have the formulas:

$$ \displaystyle\text{tr}\alpha=Ric_{44},\ \text{tr}\underline{\alpha}=Ric_{33},\ \text{tr}\tau=Ric_{34}-2\rho \displaystyle\tau_{AB}=\not{g}^{CD}R_{CADB}-Ric_{AB},\ \beta_{A}=\nu_{AB}{}^{B}+Ric_{A4},\ \underline{\beta}_{A}=-\underline{\nu}_{AB}{}^{B}-Ric_{A3}. $$

The Einstein equations are equivalent to a set of null structure equations and constraint equations involving the Ricci coefficients and the curvature components. We refer the reader to [RSR18, Section 3] for the derivation of the equations.

#### Proposition 2.1.

We have the following null structure equations for the vacuum spacetime $\big(\mathcal{M},g\big)$ :

$$ \displaystyle\nabla_{4}\text{tr}\chi+\frac{1}{n}\big(\text{tr}\chi\big)^{2} \displaystyle=-|\hat{\chi}|^{2}-2\omega\text{tr}\chi \displaystyle\nabla_{4}\hat{\chi}_{AB}+\frac{2}{n}\text{tr}\chi\hat{\chi}_{AB} \displaystyle=-\alpha_{AB}-2\omega\hat{\chi}_{AB}+\hat{\chi}\cdot\hat{\chi} \displaystyle\nabla_{3}\text{tr}\underline{\chi}+\frac{1}{n}\big(\text{tr}\underline{\chi}\big)^{2} \displaystyle=-|\hat{\underline{\chi}}|^{2}-2\underline{\omega}\text{tr}\underline{\chi} \displaystyle\nabla_{3}\hat{\underline{\chi}}_{AB}+\frac{2}{n}\text{tr}\underline{\chi}\hat{\underline{\chi}}_{AB} \displaystyle=-\underline{\alpha}_{AB}-2\underline{\omega}\hat{\underline{\chi}}_{AB}+\hat{\underline{\chi}}\cdot\hat{\underline{\chi}} \displaystyle\nabla_{3}\hat{\chi}_{AB}+\frac{1}{n}\text{tr}\underline{\chi}\hat{\chi}_{AB} \displaystyle=-\hat{\tau}_{AB}+2\underline{\omega}\hat{\chi}_{AB}+\big(\nabla\hat{\otimes}\eta\big)_{AB}-\frac{1}{n}\text{tr}\chi\underline{\hat{\chi}}_{AB}+\eta\cdot\eta+\hat{\chi}\cdot\hat{\underline{\chi}} \displaystyle\nabla_{3}\text{tr}\chi+\frac{1}{n}\text{tr}\underline{\chi}\text{tr}\chi \displaystyle=2\rho+2\underline{\omega}\text{tr}\chi+2div(\eta)+2|\eta|^{2}+\hat{\chi}\cdot\hat{\underline{\chi}} \displaystyle\nabla_{4}\hat{\underline{\chi}}_{AB}+\frac{1}{n}\text{tr}\chi\hat{\underline{\chi}}_{AB} \displaystyle=-\hat{\tau}_{AB}+2\omega\hat{\underline{\chi}}_{AB}+\big(\nabla\hat{\otimes}\underline{\eta}\big)_{AB}-\frac{1}{n}\text{tr}\underline{\chi}\hat{\chi}_{AB}+\underline{\eta}\cdot\underline{\eta}+\hat{\chi}\cdot\hat{\underline{\chi}} \displaystyle\nabla_{4}\text{tr}\underline{\chi}+\frac{1}{n}\text{tr}\underline{\chi}\text{tr}\chi \displaystyle=2\rho+2\omega\text{tr}\underline{\chi}+2div(\underline{\eta})+2|\underline{\eta}|^{2}+\hat{\chi}\cdot\hat{\underline{\chi}} \displaystyle\nabla_{4}\eta \displaystyle=-\beta+\chi\cdot(\eta-\underline{\eta}) \displaystyle\nabla_{3}\underline{\eta} \displaystyle=\underline{\beta}+\underline{\chi}\cdot(\eta-\underline{\eta})
