$$ \mathcal{L}\lesssim\epsilon\mathcal{R}+\mathcal{D}+\int_{v}^{1}(v^{\prime})^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}dv^{\prime}+\sum_{l=0}^{\frac{n-6}{2}}\sum_{m=0}^{M+\frac{n-4}{2}-l}\int_{v}^{1}\big\|Err_{m,l}^{\Psi}\big\|^{2}_{L^{2}}dv^{\prime}. $$

∎

The bounds for the remaining terms are similar to Section 8. We notice that the norms defined above control the same terms as the norms of Section 8, the only difference being the bound:

$$ \sum_{m=0}^{M}\big\|\nabla^{m}\nabla_{4}^{\frac{n-4}{2}}\alpha\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}\lesssim v^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}. $$

Due to the structure of the error terms it suffices to control only $M+1/2$ angular derivatives of $\nabla_{4}^{\frac{n-4}{2}}\alpha$ in the above bound, since the terms with more angular derivatives also have better $v$ weights. Thus, this bound replaces the use of the mildly singular top order energy in Section 8. We briefly explain the proofs for the remaining terms:

#### Proposition 10.3.

The fractional lower order energy $\mathcal{M}_{l}$ satisfies the estimate for any $0\leq l\leq\frac{n-6}{2}$ and $0\leq v\leq 1:$

$$ \mathcal{M}_{l}\lesssim v^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}+\big\|Err_{M,l}^{\Psi}\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}. $$

#### Proof.

As in Section 8, we have the estimate for any $0\leq l\leq\frac{n-6}{2}$ :

$$ \big\|\nabla^{M}\nabla_{4}^{l}\Psi\big\|^{2}_{H^{5/2}}\lesssim\mathcal{L}+\big\|v\nabla_{4}\nabla^{M}\nabla_{4}^{l+1}\Psi\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}+\big\|v\nabla_{4}\nabla^{M}\big(\psi\nabla_{4}^{l}\Psi\big)\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}+ $$

$$ +\big\|\nabla^{M}\nabla_{4}^{l+1}\Psi\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}+\big\|\nabla^{M}\big(\psi\nabla_{4}^{l}\Psi\big)\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}+\big\|Err_{M,l}^{\Psi}\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}} $$

$$ \lesssim\mathcal{L}+v^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{R}+\big\|v\nabla_{4}\nabla^{M}\nabla_{4}^{l+1}\Psi\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}+\big\|v\nabla_{4}\nabla^{M}\big(\psi\nabla_{4}^{l}\Psi\big)\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}+\big\|Err_{M,l}^{\Psi}\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}} $$

Considering separately the cases $l=\frac{n-6}{2}$ and $0\leq l\leq\frac{n-8}{2}$ , we also have as before:

$$ \big\|v\nabla_{4}\nabla^{M}\nabla_{4}^{l+1}\Psi\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}\lesssim v^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}. $$

Finally, we have the bound as in Section 8:

$$ \big\|v\nabla_{4}\nabla^{M}\big(\psi\nabla_{4}^{l}\Psi\big)\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}\lesssim\big\|v\nabla^{M}\big(\psi\nabla_{4}^{l+1}\Psi\big)\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}+\big\|v\nabla^{M}\big((\Psi+\psi\psi)\nabla_{4}^{l}\Psi\big)\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\lesssim v^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}. $$

∎

Next, we follow the same steps as in Section 8 to prove the result for the Ricci coefficients:

#### Proposition 10.4.

The Ricci coefficients norm $\mathcal{R}$ satisfies the estimate for any $0\leq v\leq 1:$

$$ \mathcal{R}\lesssim\mathcal{D}+\int_{v}^{1}\big((v^{\prime})^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}+(v^{\prime})^{1/2}\mathcal{M}_{\frac{n-6}{2}}\big)dv^{\prime}. $$

#### Proof.

Using the commuted equations satisfied by the Ricci coefficients $\psi^{*}$ , we obtain the estimate:

$$ \sum_{l=0}^{\frac{n-4}{2}}\sum_{m=0}^{M+\frac{n-4}{2}-l}\big\|\nabla_{4}^{l}\psi^{*}\big\|^{2}_{H^{m+1}}\lesssim\mathcal{D}+\sum_{l=0}^{\frac{n-4}{2}}\sum_{m=0}^{M+\frac{n-4}{2}-l}\int_{v}^{1}(v^{\prime})^{1/2}\big\|\nabla_{4}^{l}\big(\psi\psi^{*}\big)\big\|^{2}_{H^{m+1}}+(v^{\prime})^{1/2}\big\|\psi\nabla_{4}^{l}\big(\psi\psi^{*}\big)\big\|^{2}_{H^{m+1}}dv^{\prime}+ $$

$$ +\sum_{l=0}^{\frac{n-4}{2}}\sum_{m=0}^{M+\frac{n-4}{2}-l}\int_{v}^{1}(v^{\prime})^{1/2}\big\|\nabla_{4}^{l}\Psi\big\|^{2}_{H^{m+1}}dv^{\prime}\lesssim\mathcal{D}+\int_{v}^{1}\big((v^{\prime})^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\big)dv^{\prime} $$

Using the LP projections and Gronwall as before, we also obtain the following fractional estimate:

$$ \big\|\nabla^{M+1}\nabla_{4}^{\frac{n-4}{2}}\psi^{*}\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}\lesssim\mathcal{D}+\int_{v}^{1}\big((v^{\prime})^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\big)dv^{\prime}+\int_{0}^{v}(v^{\prime})^{1/2}\big\|\nabla_{4}\nabla^{M+1}\nabla_{4}^{\frac{n-4}{2}}\psi^{*}\big\|_{H^{1/2}}^{2} $$

$$ \lesssim\mathcal{D}+\int_{v}^{1}\big((v^{\prime})^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\big)dv^{\prime}+\sum_{m=0}^{M+1}\int_{v}^{1}\big\|\nabla^{m}\nabla_{4}^{\frac{n-4}{2}}\big(\psi\psi^{*}\big)\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}+(v^{\prime})^{1/2}\big\|\nabla^{m}\nabla_{4}^{\frac{n-4}{2}}\Psi\big\|_{H^{1/2}}^{2} $$

$$ \lesssim\mathcal{D}+\int_{v}^{1}\big((v^{\prime})^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\big)dv^{\prime} $$

Similarly, we also get the estimate in the case when $n\geq 6$ :

$$ \big\|\nabla^{M+2}\nabla_{4}^{\frac{n-6}{2}}\psi^{*}\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}\lesssim\mathcal{D}+\int_{v}^{1}\big((v^{\prime})^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\big)dv^{\prime}+\int_{0}^{v}(v^{\prime})^{1/2}\big\|\nabla_{4}\nabla^{M+2}\nabla_{4}^{\frac{n-6}{2}}\psi^{*}\big\|_{H^{1/2}}^{2} $$

$$ \lesssim\mathcal{D}+\int_{v}^{1}\big((v^{\prime})^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\big)dv^{\prime}+\sum_{m=0}^{M+2}\int_{0}^{v}\big\|\nabla^{m}\nabla_{4}^{\frac{n-6}{2}}\big(\psi\psi^{*}\big)\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}+(v^{\prime})^{1/2}\big\|\nabla^{m}\nabla_{4}^{\frac{n-6}{2}}\Psi\big\|_{H^{1/2}}^{2} $$

$$ \lesssim\mathcal{D}+\int_{v}^{1}(v^{\prime})^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}+(v^{\prime})^{1/2}\mathcal{M}_{\frac{n-6}{2}}. $$

∎

The remaining step in proving Proposition 10.1 is controlling the error terms from the above estimates. Since the lower order pointwise norms $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{SP}$ satisfy the same bounds as in Section 8, we get that Lemma 8.1 applies in the current situation. We adapt the proof in Section 8 to prove the following result for the error terms:

#### Proposition 10.5.

For any $0\leq l\leq\frac{n-4}{2},\ 0\leq m\leq M$ , the error terms $Err_{m,l}^{\Psi}$ satisfy the estimate:

$$ \big\|Err_{m,l}^{\Psi}\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}\lesssim\big(1+|\log(v)|^{2}\big)\big(v^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\big). $$

#### Proof.

As in Section 8, the proof follows from the fractional lower order energy estimates, once we prove the claim:

$$ \big\|Err_{m,l}^{\Psi}\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}\lesssim\big(1+|\log(v)|^{2}\big)\big(v^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\big)+\mathcal{M}_{l-1}. $$

However, the proof of this estimate follows the exact same steps as in Section 8 once we replace all the mildly singular norms $\mathcal{S}$ by $v^{-1/2}\mathcal{T},$ so we omit repeating the proof here. We then use the fractional lower order energy estimate to obtain:

$$ \big\|Err_{m,l}^{\Psi}\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}\lesssim\big(1+|\log(v)|^{2}\big)\big(v^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\big)+\mathcal{M}_{l-1}\lesssim\big(1+|\log(v)|^{2}\big)\big(v^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\big)+\big\|Err_{m,l-1}^{\Psi}\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}} $$

By induction we obtain that:

$$ \big\|Err_{m,l}^{\Psi}\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}\lesssim\big(1+|\log(v)|^{2}\big)\big(v^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\big)+\big\|Err_{m,0}^{\Psi}\big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}\lesssim\big(1+|\log(v)|^{2}\big)\big(v^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\big). $$

∎

Similarly, we can repeat the proof in Section 8 and replace the mildly singular norms $\mathcal{S}$ by $v^{-1/2}\mathcal{T},$ in order to establish the following result for the remaining error terms:

#### Proposition 10.6.

For any for any $0\leq l\leq\frac{n-4}{2}$ and $0\leq m\leq M+\frac{n-4}{2}-l$ , the error terms $Err_{m,l}^{\Psi}$ satisfy the estimate:

$$ \big\|Err_{m,l}^{\Psi}\big\|^{2}_{L^{2}}\lesssim(1+|\log(v)|^{2}\big)\big(v^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\big). $$

We complete the proofs of Proposition 10.1 and Theorem 10.1:

Proof of Proposition 10.1. Using the estimates in this section, we have that for all $0\leq v\leq 1$ :

$$ \mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\lesssim\mathcal{D}+\epsilon\mathcal{R}+\int_{v}^{1}\big(1+|\log v^{\prime}|^{2}\big)\big((v^{\prime})^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\big)dv^{\prime}. $$

Taking $\epsilon>0$ small enough and using Gronwall’s inequality, we conclude that $\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\lesssim\mathcal{D}.$ ∎

Proof of Theorem 10.1. In order to complete the proof of Theorem 10.1, we prove the bound:

$$ \big\|\not{g}_{0}^{*}\big\|_{\mathring{H}^{M+1}}^{2}+\big\|\mathcal{O}\big\|_{H^{M+1}}^{2}+\big\|\mathfrak{h}\big\|_{H^{M+1}}^{2}\lesssim\mathcal{D}, $$

since the other terms in the asymptotic data norm $\big\|\Sigma\big\|_{M}^{2}$ are already bounded by $\mathcal{D}$ using Proposition 10.1. Using the estimates on the asymptotic data in Theorem 9.2 we obtain:

$$ \big\|\mathcal{O}\big\|_{H^{M+1}}^{2}\lesssim\mathcal{D}+\sum_{m=0}^{M}\int_{0}^{1}\Big\|Err_{m,\frac{n-4}{2}}^{\Psi}\Big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}dv. $$

We also use the above estimates on the error terms and Proposition 10.1:

$$ \big\|\mathcal{O}\big\|_{H^{M+1}}^{2}\lesssim\mathcal{D}+\int_{0}^{1}\big(1+|\log(v)|^{2}\big)\big(v^{-1/2}\mathcal{T}+\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{R}\big)dv\lesssim\mathcal{D}. $$

Using the metric equation $\mathcal{L}_{v}\not{g}^{*}=\psi^{*}$ and the estimate $\mathcal{R}\lesssim\mathcal{D},$ we obtain that $\big\|\not{g}^{*}\big\|_{H^{M+1}}^{2}\lesssim\mathcal{D}.$ We use this, together with the estimates in Proposition 3.3 and (3.3) in order to prove by induction on $m\leq M+1$ that $\big\|\mathcal{L}_{\theta}^{m}\not{g}_{0}^{*}\big\|_{L^{2}(S^{n})}^{2}\lesssim\epsilon.$ In particular, this allows us to bound the Christoffel symbols terms in (3.3) and prove:

$$ \sum_{m\leq M+1}\big\|\mathcal{L}_{\theta}^{m}\not{g}_{0}^{*}\big\|_{L^{2}(S^{n})}^{2}\lesssim\mathcal{D} $$

We can then use (3.3) for covariant derivatives with respect to $\not{g}_{S^{n}}$ and prove by induction on $m\leq M+1$ that:

$$ \big\|\mathring{\nabla}^{m}\not{g}^{*}_{0}\big\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\lesssim\mathcal{D}. $$

In order to complete the proof of (10.1), we must bound $\big\|\mathfrak{h}\big\|_{H^{M+1}}.$ By Theorem 9.2 we get:

$$ \big\|\mathfrak{h}\big\|_{H^{M+1}}^{2}\lesssim\mathcal{D}+\big\|h\big\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+C\Big(\big\|\not{Riem}_{0}\big\|_{H^{M}}^{2}\Big)\big\|\mathcal{O}\big\|_{H^{M}}^{2}+\sum_{m=0}^{M}\int_{0}^{1}\Big\|Err_{m,\frac{n-4}{2}}^{\Psi}\Big\|^{2}_{H^{1/2}}dv\lesssim\mathcal{D}+\big\|h\big\|_{L^{2}}^{2}, $$

where we used the constraint $\not{Riem}=R+\psi\psi$ and the previously established bounds for $\mathcal{O}$ and the error terms. For the rest of the proof we prove a suitable lower order estimate for $\big\|h\big\|_{L^{2}}^{2}.$ As in the proof of Theorem 9.2, we define $\xi=\nabla_{4}^{\frac{n-4}{2}}\alpha$ and $\overline{\xi}=\xi-v\log v\nabla_{4}\xi.$ We compute using (5.9):

$$ \nabla_{4}\overline{\xi}=-\log v\cdot\nabla_{4}\big(v\nabla_{4}\xi\big)=\log v\cdot\Big(\Delta\nabla_{4}^{\frac{n-4}{2}}\alpha+\psi\nabla\nabla_{4}^{\frac{n-4}{2}}\Psi+Err^{\Psi}_{0,\frac{n-4}{2}}\Big). $$

Therefore, we get using our previous estimates:

$$ \big\|h\big\|_{L^{2}}^{2}=\lim_{v\rightarrow 0}\big\|\overline{\xi}\big\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\lesssim\mathcal{D}+\int_{0}^{1}(\log v)^{2}\cdot\Big(\big\|\nabla_{4}^{\frac{n-4}{2}}\Psi\big\|_{H^{2}}^{2}+\big\|Err^{\Psi}_{0,\frac{n-4}{2}}\big\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\Big)\lesssim\mathcal{D}. $$

This completes the proof of Theorem 10.1. ∎

## 11 The Scattering Map

In this section, we follow the outline in Section 1.3.3 of the introduction and we put together our previous results in order to complete the proof of the third statement in Theorem 1.3. For any $M>0$ large enough and $\epsilon>0$ small enough we consider smooth straight initial data $\big(\not{g}_{0},h\big)$ such that the corresponding asymptotic data set satisfies $\Sigma\big(\not{g}_{0},h\big)\in B_{\epsilon}^{M}\big(\Sigma_{\mathrm{Minkowski}}\big).$ By Theorem 3.1 there exists a unique smooth straight self-similar vacuum solution $(\mathcal{M},g)$ in double null coordinates defined in $\{u<0,\ v>0\}$ with asymptotic initial data at $\{v=0\}$ given by $\big(\not{g}_{0},h\big).$ Moreover, this induces smooth asymptotic data $\big(\underline{\not{g}_{0}},\underline{h}\big)$ at $\{u=0\}$ by Theorem 4.1. The estimates in Theorem 8.1 imply that:

$$ \Xi_{M}\lesssim\Big\|\Sigma\big(\not{g}_{0},h\big)\Big\|_{M}. $$

We also have by Theorem 10.1 that the reverse inequality holds. We use this inequality for the spacetime obtained by reversing the time orientation, namely by replacing $(u,v)$ with $(-v,-u)$ . We obtain the estimate:

$$ \Big\|\Sigma\big(\underline{\not{g}_{0}},\underline{h}\big)\Big\|_{M}\lesssim\Xi_{M}, $$

where $\Sigma\big(\underline{\not{g}_{0}},\underline{h}\big)$ is defined according to Remark 8.1. Therefore, there exists a constant $C_{M}>0$ depending only on $M$ such that:

$$ \Big\|\Sigma\big(\underline{\not{g}_{0}},\underline{h}\big)\Big\|_{M}\leq C_{M}\Big\|\Sigma\big(\not{g}_{0},h\big)\Big\|_{M}. $$

We obtain that $\Sigma\big(\underline{\not{g}_{0}},\underline{h}\big)\in B_{C_{M}\epsilon}^{M}\big(\Sigma_{\mathrm{Minkowski}}\big),$ so we can define the scattering map:

$$ \mathcal{S}:B_{\epsilon}^{M}\big(\Sigma_{\mathrm{Minkowski}}\big)\rightarrow B_{C_{M}\epsilon}^{M}\big(\Sigma_{\mathrm{Minkowski}}\big),\ \mathcal{S}\big(\Sigma(\not{g}_{0},h)\big)=\Sigma(\underline{\not{g}_{0}},\underline{h}). $$

Using the uniqueness of scattering states statement from Theorem 3.1, we obtain that $\mathcal{S}$ is injective. Moreover, we can apply the existence and uniqueness results, together with the estimate (1.12) in the reverse time direction to obtain that $B_{\epsilon/C_{M}}^{M}\big(\Sigma_{\mathrm{Minkowski}}\big)\subset\mathcal{S}\big(B_{\epsilon}^{M}(\Sigma_{\mathrm{Minkowski}})\big).$ Therefore, $\mathcal{S}$ is locally invertible at $\Sigma_{\mathrm{Minkowski}}.$ Finally, the above estimate implies that $\mathcal{S}$ is locally Lipschitz at $\Sigma_{\mathrm{Minkowski}}.$
